About

Fisherman's son, minister, national office-bearer

ಪರಿಚಯ

Born in 1968 in Udupi, he grew up in a family of public servants. His father Malpe Madhwaraj built Malpe harbour. He became a first-time MLA in 2013 and went on to hold three portfolios in the Karnataka government.

First fisherman minister

The first person from the fishing community to head Karnataka's Fisheries department.

Ranked No. 1 of 224

Top of the March 2018 performance survey of Karnataka MLAs by Times of India and Prajavani.

Udupi District In-charge

Served as the district's In-charge Minister, alongside Fisheries, Youth Empowerment and Sports.

National General Secretary

Appointed on 21 Nov 2026 to the BJP OBC Morcha, to represent backward and fishing communities.

Journey

Udupi to the national stage

ಜೀವನ ಪಯಣ

  1. 1968

    Born in Udupi, into a family already part of the district's public life.

  2. Early years

    Youth leadership in student and youth politics.

  3. 2013

    Elected MLA for Udupi, as a first-time legislator.

  4. 2015

    Appointed Parliamentary Secretary (Revenue).

  5. 2016

    Became Minister of State, then Cabinet Minister for Fisheries, Youth Empowerment and Sports under Chief Minister Siddaramaiah. Also Udupi District In-charge Minister.

  6. March 2018

    Ranked No. 1 among 224 MLAs in a Times of India / Prajavani survey.

  7. 12 May 2018

    Contested the Udupi Assembly election, with a constituency progress booklet published ahead of polling.

  8. 7 May 2022

    Joined the BJP.

  9. 2023

    Campaigned across 13 constituencies in the Karnataka Assembly election.

  10. 21 Nov 2026

    Appointed National General Secretary of the BJP OBC Morcha, to organise OBC Morcha units and represent backward and fishing communities.

By the numbers

Five years in figures

ಐದು ವರ್ಷಗಳ ಸಾಧನೆ

Headline counts from a 2018 booklet on Udupi constituency, 2013–18.

Fisheries and ports · ₹433 crore

Fishermen first

ಮೀನುಗಾರಿಕೆ

The largest-ever push for the coast: higher subsidies and relief for boat owners and fisherwomen, a bigger Malpe harbour, and India's largest women's fish market.

Before and after

What changed for fishing families during his tenure.

Harbour and coast works

₹ crore, as listed in the booklet. Some items were proposals.

Reaching boat owners and families

  • ₹254.13 crore in diesel subsidy reached 1,622 boat owners in the constituency.
  • Sales-tax-free diesel per boat raised from 1.25 to 1.50 lakh kL, with the subsidy paid by RTGS to bank accounts.
  • 163 illegally built mechanised boats regularised, and feasibility-letter rules simplified.
  • Matsyashraya housing aid reached 368 fisher families: ₹3.19 crore.
  • 29,789 fisherwomen got cheaper loans of ₹50,000: ₹16 crore in two years.
  • 34 families of fishermen lost at sea received relief.
  • A Deputy Director of Fisheries office opened in Udupi, which earlier depended on Mangaluru.

Malpe harbour, phase by phase

  • Phase 3 at Baputhota gives berthing for 700+ boats.
  • A mechanical slipway built with Tebma Shipyard, for repairing boats.
  • A 75 m jetty at Malpe: ₹2.40 crore. Phase 1 and 2 upgrade: ₹5 crore. Dredging: ₹7.75 crore.
  • Padukere 250 m jetty and Bobbarya Pade jetty extension: ₹11.30 crore (NABARD proposal). A further 300 m jetty at Padukere: ₹9.6 crore.
  • Commercial port jetty extension of 50 m (₹5 crore plus ₹0.80 crore), with a 100 m extension (₹9.60 crore) proposed.
  • Udupi's old fish market rebuilt as India's largest women's fish market: ₹2.30 crore, about 200 women vendors.
  • 28.80 km of fisheries roads: ₹4.876 crore (NABARD and department funds).

Infrastructure

Bridges, roads and the city

ಸೇತುವೆ · ರಸ್ತೆ · ಉಡುಪಿ ನಗರ

Bridges · ₹84 crore

Cost of the bigger bridges

₹ crore. The Malpe–Padukere bridge is 315 m long and ended about 60 years of dependence on boats.

More crossings

  • Kallianka widening: ₹0.75 crore.
  • Kodankur Babbuswami mini-bridge: ₹0.50 crore.
  • Kambalakatta bridge: ₹0.25 crore.
  • Several Sita-river road bridges and vented dams, each between ₹0.15 and ₹0.90 crore.
  • Funding came through Amrut Mahotsav, Nagarotthana, State Finance Commission, CRF and KRDCL.

Roads · ₹468 crore

3,348 road works sanctioned

The largest single sector, across PWD, CRF, Namma Grama Namma Raste, PMGSY, Nagarotthana-3, the coastal authority and SC/ST colony roads.

By number of works
Completed: 2,695 works, ₹286.48 crIn progress: 653 works, ₹182.52 cr
By length (788 km sanctioned)
Completed: 573 kmIn progress: 215 km

National Highway 66

  • ₹118.14 crore for the highway in the constituency.
  • Drains, roads and bridges along NH-66: ₹46.50 crore.
  • ₹71.64 crore in compensation paid to 872 landowners.

Udupi city · ₹445 crore

Water for the city

The Varahi to Baje scheme more than doubles capacity. Total about ₹270 crore, within ₹370 crore of ADB and AMRUT drinking water and drainage works.

23MLD before
43MLD with the new scheme

Other city funds

Homes and tourism

  • About 500 house sites at Lingotigudde, Kodange and Sannakkibettu.
  • Pramod Madhwaraj Badavane at Kodankur: 33 houses for Sudugadu Siddha and Budaga Jangama nomads.
  • Tourism, ₹16.70 crore: a 450 m walkway behind the shipyard (₹54.09 lakh).
  • Malpe beach: toilets, a beach-cleaning machine, granite benches and free Wi-Fi.
  • 36 tourist taxis worth ₹0.72 crore, plus facilities at Mannapalla, Manipal.
  • Malpe beach road ₹2.20 crore, and Nalkur to Joma Theertha falls road ₹2.10 crore.
  • Santhekatte commercial complex: ₹1.92 crore.
  • Nagarotthana-3 works included a four-lane Ambagilu to Kallianka road (₹4.50 crore).

Farms, sports and youth

Fields, tanks and the stadium

ಕೃಷಿ · ಕ್ರೀಡೆ

Agriculture and allied · ₹71 crore

Where it went

₹ crore.

Farmers and dairy

  • Milk incentive of ₹2 to ₹4 per litre paid to 13,197 dairy farmers: ₹26.16 crore.
  • Animal husbandry spending in all: ₹27 crore, with 403 beneficiaries under Pashu Bhagya and related schemes.
  • Low-interest loans reached 385 farmers (₹2.44 crore), plus a farm loan waiver of ₹1.38 crore.
  • 46 power tillers distributed: ₹26.23 lakh.
  • Raitha Samparka Kendra opened at Adi Udupi. Lakes at Mannapalla (₹1.45 crore) and Chanthar Madaga (₹1 crore) restored.
  • Areca disease relief for 1,007 farmers: ₹0.71 crore.

Youth and sports · ₹25.99 crore

Ajjarkad stadium, upgraded

₹ crore.

A host for state events

  • Udupi hosted a national women's sports meet, state rural sports three times, a state youth mela three times and a state youth fest.
  • Sports hostel upgraded to PU level, with athletics and swimming academies.
  • Brahmavar cricket ground on 5.5 acres, with a wall costing ₹75 lakh.
  • Two acres at Malpe Padukere set aside for water sports.
  • The Yuva Chaitanya scheme supports youth clubs.
  • The pavilion roof (₹83 lakh) came from an MP's local area fund.
  • The State's first Sports Policy and first State Inland Fisheries Policy were introduced during his tenure as minister.

    Malpe Madhwaraj

    Manorama Madhwaraj
